document: HomeGuard Privacy Platform — Mailwatcher Service Specification
description: Autonomous service that polls the dedicated removal email inbox via IMAP, parses and classifies inbound broker responses, links emails to removal requests, extracts verification links for automatic opt-out completion, and dispatches Celery tasks to update request status.

design_decisions.classification_engine: Keyword + regex hybrid — keyword pre-filter eliminates irrelevant emails cheaply, regex handles broker response phrasing variations
design_decisions.request_matching: Sender domain + subject line combined — higher confidence than domain alone, handles brokers that send from multiple domains
design_decisions.post_processing: Move to IMAP 'Processed' folder — preserves emails for human review and re-processing, prevents duplicate processing
design_decisions.verification_links: Mailwatcher automatically extracts verification URLs and dispatches Celery task to trigger Playwright click — maintains fully-automatic design

IMAP_INBOX_FOLDER.description: Folder to poll for new messages

IMAP_PROCESSED_FOLDER.description: Folder messages are moved to after processing. Created automatically if it does not exist.

IMAP_ERROR_FOLDER.description: Folder for messages that caused exceptions during processing

CELERY_BROKER_URL.description: Redis URL for dispatching Celery tasks

INTERNAL_API_URL.description: Base URL for internal API calls

INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN.description: Shared secret for internal API auth

mailwatcher/.main.py: Entry point — poll loop, graceful shutdown handler
mailwatcher/.imap_client.py: IMAPClient class — connection, polling, folder management
mailwatcher/.email_parser.py: EmailParser class — extract sender, subject, body, links
mailwatcher/.classifier.py: EmailClassifier class — keyword pre-filter + regex classification
mailwatcher/.request_matcher.py: RequestMatcher class — link email to removal_request in DB
mailwatcher/.link_extractor.py: VerificationLinkExtractor class — detect and extract opt-out verification URLs
mailwatcher/.dispatcher.py: TaskDispatcher class — write to DB and dispatch Celery tasks
mailwatcher/.requirements.txt: imaplib2, beautifulsoup4, pyyaml, sqlalchemy, celery, pydantic, aiofiles, lxml

poll_loop.description: Main execution loop — runs continuously while the container is alive
cycle: 1. Connect to IMAP server (reconnect if connection dropped)
4. For each unseen message UID: fetch headers + body
6. Deduplicate via message_id_header check against mail.inbound_messages
8. Pass ParsedEmail + ClassificationResult to RequestMatcher → MatchResult
9. If verification link detected: pass to VerificationLinkExtractor
10. Pass all results to TaskDispatcher → write DB + dispatch Celery tasks
11. Move message to IMAP Processed folder (or Error folder on exception)

connection_resilience.note: Cap of 50 prevents memory spike if inbox accumulates during downtime

imap_folder_management.processed_folder_creation: On startup: attempt IMAP CREATE Processed. Ignore error if already exists.
imap_folder_management.error_folder_creation: Same as Processed — created on startup
imap_folder_management.move_operation: IMAP COPY uid Processed; IMAP STORE uid +FLAGS (\Deleted); IMAP EXPUNGE

email_parser.description: Converts raw IMAP message bytes into a structured ParsedEmail object

parsed_email_model.from_domain: str — extracted domain from From address (e.g. spokeo.com)
parsed_email_model.from_name: str | None — display name if present
parsed_email_model.subject: str
parsed_email_model.raw_body_html: str | None — HTML body if no plain text alternative
parsed_email_model.body_text_normalised: str — lowercase, whitespace-collapsed body for matching
parsed_email_model.links: list[str] — all URLs extracted from body (both text and HTML parts)

body_extraction.html_fallback: If only HTML body: strip tags via BeautifulSoup get_text() with separator=' '
body_extraction.encoding: Decode with detected charset, fallback to utf-8, fallback to latin-1

link_extraction.from_html: BeautifulSoup find_all('a', href=True) applied to raw_body_html

classifier.description: Two-stage classifier — keyword pre-filter then regex pattern matching per classification type

classification_types.confirmed_removal: Broker confirmed the profile has been or will be removed
classification_types.rejection: Broker denied or cannot process the removal request
classification_types.info_requested: Broker needs additional information or identity verification before processing
classification_types.verification_link: Email contains a link that must be clicked to complete the opt-out
classification_types.unclassified: No pattern matched — requires human review

classification_result_model.confidence: float 0.0-1.0 — based on number of patterns matched

stage_1_keyword_prefilter.description: Fast O(n) check against lowercase body. If no keyword matches, classify as unclassified immediately without running regex engine.
stage_1_keyword_prefilter.purpose: Eliminate irrelevant emails (spam, marketing from broker domains) cheaply
stage_1_keyword_prefilter.keyword_sources: All keywords from all classification types in patterns.yml combined into a single set
stage_1_keyword_prefilter.implementation: prefilter_keywords = set(); matched = any(kw in normalised_body for kw in prefilter_keywords)

stage_2_regex_matching.description: For emails that pass the keyword pre-filter, apply regex patterns per classification type in priority order
stage_2_regex_matching.note: verification_link checked first because some verification emails also contain confirmed_removal language
stage_2_regex_matching.multi_classification: All types above threshold are scored. Highest confidence wins. Tie broken by priority_order.

patterns_file.description: YAML file defining all classification patterns. Editable without code changes or image rebuild.

format.structure: Top-level keys per classification type. Each has keywords (list) and patterns (list of regex strings).
format.flags: All regex patterns compiled with re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL
format.reload: Patterns file is reloaded on each poll cycle — live updates without container restart

patterns_file.adding_patterns: To add broker-specific patterns, add a broker_overrides section keyed by broker domain. These patterns are checked first before global patterns for emails from that domain.

request_matcher.description: Links a parsed email to the most likely removal_request in the database using sender domain + subject line matching

match_result_model.request_id: UUID | None — None if no match found
match_result_model.match_notes: str — debug info about why this match was chosen

step_1_domain_match.description: Extract sender domain from from_domain. Look up broker by canonical_domain.
step_1_domain_match.query: SELECT id FROM registry.brokers WHERE canonical_domain ILIKE '%{from_domain}%' OR contact_email ILIKE '%{from_domain}%'
step_1_domain_match.result: List of matching broker_ids (usually 1, occasionally 0 or 2+)

step_2_subject_match.description: For each matching broker, find pending removal requests and score subject line similarity
step_2_subject_match.query: SELECT id, profile_id FROM requests.removal_requests WHERE broker_id = %s AND status IN ('submitted','pending_confirmation') ORDER BY submitted_at DESC LIMIT 10
step_2_subject_match.subject_scoring: Normalise both subject_normalised and stored request subject. Count shared tokens. Score = shared_tokens / max(len(subject_tokens), len(request_subject_tokens)).
step_2_subject_match.threshold: Accept match if subject_score >= 0.3 OR domain_match is unique (only one pending request for this broker)

step_3_confidence_calculation.domain_only: 0.5 — accepted when broker has exactly one pending request
step_3_confidence_calculation.subject_only: 0.3 — fallback when domain not in registry

matching_algorithm.ambiguous_match: If multiple requests score similarly (within 0.1 of each other), pick most recent submitted_at. Log ambiguity warning.

verification_link_extractor.description: Detects verification links in emails and automatically dispatches Celery task to click them via the Playwright executor

link_scoring.description: Score each URL extracted from the email body to find the verification link
positive_indicators: URL query params contain: token=, key=, confirm=, verify=, code=
URL domain matches from_domain of the email
URL appears in close proximity to verification keywords in body
negative_indicators: URL is an image/tracking pixel (ends in .png, .jpg, .gif, .ico, 1x1)
URL domain is a common email service (mailchimp.com, sendgrid.net, etc.)
URL is an unsubscribe link for the removal mailbox itself
link_scoring.selection: Highest scoring URL selected. If tie: first URL in body wins.

automatic_dispatch.description: Once verification link is extracted, dispatch Celery task to continue the opt-out flow via Playwright
automatic_dispatch.link_token: URL stored in profile_tokens as {email_verification_link} — passed to Playwright for the email_loop phase navigate action

click_verification_link_task.description: Celery task that receives a verification URL, creates a targeted Playwright job to click it, then awaits the optout completion
implementation_notes: Build a minimal single-phase playbook: { phases: [{ phase: verify, steps: [{ action: navigate, value: {email_verification_link} }, { action: wait_for_text, patterns: confirmation_patterns }] }] }
On confirmed: update request.status=pending_confirmation, log audit_log: verification_link_clicked
On failed: set request.status=requires_manual, create action_required notification with raw email body

task_dispatcher.description: Writes processing results to the database and dispatches appropriate Celery tasks

info_requested: Dispatch create_notification.delay(type=action_required, body includes raw email body)
unclassified: INSERT mail.message_classifications with classification=unclassified, request_id=null if no match
Dispatch create_notification.delay(type=action_required, title=Unclassified email received, body=raw email summary)

task_dispatcher.database_writes: Direct SQLAlchemy sync session (mailwatcher runs synchronously — no async needed)
task_dispatcher.celery_dispatch: Celery tasks dispatched via celery.send_task() with broker URL from CELERY_BROKER_URL

deduplication.description: Prevents the same email being processed twice — critical if container restarts or poll overlaps
deduplication.method: Check mail.inbound_messages for existing row with matching message_id_header BEFORE processing
deduplication.query: SELECT id FROM mail.inbound_messages WHERE message_id_header = %s
deduplication.on_duplicate: Skip processing entirely. Log debug: duplicate message_id skipped. Move to Processed folder.
deduplication.fallback: If email has no Message-ID header: generate a deterministic ID from SHA256(from_address + date + subject)

error_handling.parse_error: Log error with raw UID. Move message to IMAP_ERROR_FOLDER. Continue poll cycle.
error_handling.db_write_error: Log error with full context. Retry up to 3 times with 5s delay. On failure: leave in INBOX (will be re-processed next poll).
error_handling.celery_dispatch_error: Log error. Task dispatch is best-effort — DB writes already committed. Create action_required notification via direct DB insert as fallback.
error_handling.imap_connection_error: Log and reconnect with exponential backoff. Poll cycle resumes after reconnect.
error_handling.no_match_found: Classification and raw body still stored. Unclassified notification created. Not an error.

logging.format: Structured JSON to stdout — compatible with Docker json-file log driver

schema.ignore_senders: list[str] — domains to never process (e.g. noreply@mailchimp.com)
schema.verification_link_negative_domains: list[str] — URL domains to exclude from link scoring

patterns_file_full_spec.reload_behaviour: File stat()d on each poll cycle. If mtime changed: reload and recompile all regex patterns. Zero-downtime pattern updates.
patterns_file_full_spec.validation: On load: compile all regex patterns — raise ValueError with pattern and error if any fail to compile

startup_sequence: 1. Load and validate patterns.yml — compile all regex patterns
2. Connect to IMAP server with SSL
3. Create IMAP Processed and ProcessingErrors folders if absent
4. Verify DB connection via SQLAlchemy ping
5. Verify Celery broker connection via redis-py ping
6. Log startup: { service: mailwatcher, imap_host, poll_interval_seconds, patterns_loaded: N }

health_indicators.reported_to: GET http://api:8000/api/system/health via internal API call

metrics.last_poll_at: ISO datetime of last successful poll completion
metrics.consecutive_errors: integer — reset to 0 on successful poll
